bitter-sweet-a-poem: Josiah Gilbert Holland's long narrative poem in blank verse tells a story of love, loss, and consolation. Written in the elevated style Victorian readers loved, it moves between tender domestic scenes and larger reflections on sorrow and hope. The poem was a bestseller in its day, read aloud in parlors across America.
a-heart-song-of-to-day-disturbed-by-fire: Annie Gregg Savigny's Canadian novel sings a heart-song of today, disturbed by political fire from the unruly member. Love and parliament mingle in this spirited tale. A lively voice from early Canadian fiction. Ottawa drawing rooms and parliamentary sparks enliven this Canadian romance.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ad-apostolica: This 1913 reference article on Ad Apostolicae Dignitatis Apicem — Innocent IV's bull deposing Frederick II. Michael O'Riordan tells of Lyons in 1245. Pope and emperor clashed in open council. The boldest stroke of the medieval papacy. Frederick called it the pope's mad bull. The empire never recovered the blow.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ad-sanctam-be: This 1913 reference piece on Ad Sanctam Beati Petri Sedem — Pius IX's letter inviting the Eastern Churches to unity. Michael O'Riordan gives its occasion. Rome stretched out a hand in 1848. An olive branch to the East. The East answered with polite reserve. The dream of reunion lived on.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-afflighem: A 1913 entry on Afflighem — the Belgian abbey of Brabant's dukes. Henry Brock tells its long story. Its monks kept the old Benedictine rule. War and time tested its walls. A venerable house of the Low Countries. Its brewery kept the old monastic craft.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ancient-see-o: A 1913 entry on the ancient see of Trondhjem — Nidaros, Norway's primatial see. Gustav Armfelt honors its glory. St. Olaf's shrine drew all the north. Its archbishops crowned the kings. The Canterbury of Norway. Its octagon holds the high altar. Its bells rang for seven centuries.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-assizes-of-je: A 1913 entry on the Assizes of Jerusalem — the crusaders' feudal code. Charles Moeller unfolds its baronial law. The High Court judged the kingdom. The laws of Outremer bound the Franks. The jurisprudence of the Latin East. Their text survives in Cypriot copies.
